thread:
pagerbot: ALERT: High tail latency + 429s observed in eu-west-1 GPU pool -- paging oncall (ops_lead)
pagerbot: Severity: P1 — immediate attention required
ops_lead: paging @sara @alex oncall, please acknowledge
sara: ack, I'm on it
alex: ack, grabbing dashboards and logs now
sara: tl;dr: queue depth for gpu-pool-eu-west-1 jumped from ~200 -> ~5k in ~3m. Autoscaler returned scale_limit_reached and did not provision more shards. Many requests started 429'ing
mike: pasting control-plane tail logs:
```
2026-03-15T11:02:04Z control-plane autoscaler: request failed: max_pool_shards=32 reached
2026-03-15T11:02:05Z routing: response 429 token-throttle
2026-03-15T11:02:06Z serving runtime: prefixcache miss rate spike: 98% (prefixttl=0)
2026-03-15T11:02:07Z batching: continuous_batch_window_ms=10 applied (previously 80ms)
```
sara: both the prefix-cache miss storm and the batching window change line up with a roll at ~11:00. checking gitops history now
sara: found two deploys at 11:00: batching-optimizer v2 and prefix-cache config change (ttl_seconds=0)
ops_lead: ttl_seconds=0 -> effectively disables prefix caching. combined with a much smaller batch window that will crater batching efficiency. Bad interaction
alex: confirmed: decreased batching window -> fewer requests batched -> more per-token work. disabled prefix cache -> each request re-reads full KV -> backend load skyrockets. Autoscaler tried to scale but hit account shard cap
sara: immediate mitigation plan: 1) revert prefix-cache ttl to 360s 2) rollback batching-optimizer v2 to restore continuous_batch_window_ms=80 3) temporarily relax autoscaler soft_limit / request cloud quota bump if needed
ops_lead: @deploy-bot kick revert for prefix-cache (high priority)
deploy-bot: Revert PR created (#9412) for prefix-cache ttl -> queued for CI at 11:08
sara: while CI runs, do a per-shard concurrency increase and set autoscaler.soft_limit=false to allow temporary overprovisioning
mike: issuing commands to adjust runtime knobs (applied):
```
# increase per-shard concurrency
curl -X POST https://admin.api/runtime/adjust -d '{"pool":"gpu-pool-eu-west-1","max_concurrency_per_shard":1.5}'
# disable soft limit
curl -X POST https://admin.api/autoscaler/adjust -d '{"soft_limit":false}'
```
alex: cloud quota request opened for pool_shards increase, but approval ETA unknown. rolling back cache should remove need for quota bump if effective quickly
sara: metrics snapshot during incident window:
```
11:00 queue_depth: 220
11:03 queue_depth: 5200
11:05 5xx rate delta: +0.8%
11:06 429 rate delta: +3.4%
11:10 prefix_cache_hit: 2%
11:20 prefix_cache_hit: 72% (post-revert)
```
ops_lead: customer impact: hosted API customers in eu-west-1 saw higher latency and some 429s between ~11:01-11:15 UTC. Support notified, comms in-flight
support: multiple tickets received about 429s in that window. tagging affected tenants and prioritizing responses
alex: revert PR merged at 11:11, deploy started 11:12
deploy-bot: Deploy: prefix-cache revert -> rollout 100% complete at 11:18
mike: after prefix revert, prefix_cache_hit rose to ~72% by 11:20, queue started falling but batching window still low (10ms) because batching-optimizer rollback pending
sara: initiating rollback of batching-optimizer at 11:19 (canary 10%)
deploy-bot: Batching-optimizer rollback completed at 11:27 (100%)
alex: by 11:30 queue_depth back to ~180, 429s normalized, latencies recovered to baseline
ops_lead: autoscaler soft_limit toggle and per-shard concurrency were temporary band-aids; primary fix was config reverts. Cloud quota not needed after reverts
sara: root cause summary for follow-up: simultaneous rollouts — prefix cache ttl=0 + batching-optimizer v2 (reduced continuous batching window) created a negative interaction that removed caching and reduced batching efficiency, driving increased load. Autoscaler surfaced a cap (max_pool_shards) and could not catch up
mike: follow-ups: - add pre-deploy gate: disallow prefix-cache ttl=0 in prod unless explicitly flagged - require pairing of batching param changes with cache config in a single changelist and a canary acceptance check - add alert on autoscaler.scale_limit_reached with paging to infra-sre - create test harness to simulate cache-miss + small-batch window scenario
ops_lead: assigning owners: gating + schema validation -> sara; autoscaler alerting -> infra-sre; canary checks -> alex; overflow pool plan -> mike
infra-sre: taking autoscaler alerting ticket, will collect detailed logs and provide analysis and timeline for postmortem. planning PM draft by EOD
ops_lead: comms: ops status update and affected tenant list will be posted to #incidents-communications in 30m. support to follow up with tenant notices
sara: one-line RCA to include in comms: simultaneous deployment of batching-optimizer v2 (reduced batching window) and a prefix-cache TTL misconfiguration (ttl=0) caused cache miss storm and loss of effective batching, overwhelming provisioned GPU shards and triggering client throttles
alex: also adding to RCA: deployment approvals should flag multi-component runtime-impacting changes and require explicit compatibility check
ops_lead: thanks team. handing off to infra-sre for formal postmortem. closing incident thread once PM posted. :white_check_mark:
